literal_source_claim_en: The relationship between multiple and iterated integrals.
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: Under source-selected integrability and measurability hypotheses, a multiple integral over a product or planar region agrees with one or both iterated integrals, with every domain, measure, exceptional-section, and codomain convention stated explicitly.
statement_blocker: The catalog gloss does not select Lebesgue, Bochner, or Riemann integration; a planar region or product measure; scalar or Banach-valued codomain; finite, sigma-finite, or s-finite measures; product integrability or another absolute-integrability package; product-to-iterated equality, both iterated orders, or order swap; section measurability and almost-everywhere integrability; ordered binders; conclusion; or boundary cases. The JFM review and pinned mathlib provide strong but differently scoped candidates. Selecting one before primary-source review and checked transports would narrow, broaden, or substitute the received claim.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix a planar region or two measurable spaces, their measures and finiteness classes, a scalar or normed-space-valued function, universe levels, and all measurability, normed-group, scalar-action, completeness, separability, and product-measure structures.
conclusion: Prospective family only: the source-selected multiple or product integral equals one or both source-selected iterated integrals; whether section-integrability conclusions and order swap belong to the root is unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; zero or infinite measures, empty or null regions, zero and a.e.-zero functions, exceptional sections, incomplete codomains, existing iterated integrals without product integrability, nonmeasurable sections, product-measure order, and extended-valued versus finite integrals must all be resolved.
